docs.title: zer0sh Dotfiles
docs.text:
Welcome to the official documentation for zer0sh's desktop environment, built on Hyprland (Wayland) and customized with Quickshell, Waybar, Kitty / Alacritty, and Zsh.

Quick Install View Repository

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text:
• Strict Modularity

    No monolithic configuration files. Every concern (keybindings, monitor layouts, animations, autostart services) is isolated into its own dedicated file.

  • Direct Live Source of Truth

    The live Hyprland configuration resides directly in ~/.config/hypr/ as a real, independent directory, allowing seamless live edits without symlink friction.

  • Cohesive Visual Integration

    Centralized palettes generated across Quickshell, Hyprland borders, Waybar, and terminal emulators.

  • Fluid Modern OSDs & Notifications

    Floating surfaces anchored at the top-center of the screen, featuring smooth downward slide-in transitions and fluid stack displacement.

docs.title: Bat Syntax Pager & Cat Clone
docs.text: bat is a modern replacement for the traditional Unix cat command, enhanced with syntax highlighting for hundreds of programming and markup languages, Git modification badges, automatic terminal detection, and customizable paging styles.

docs.title: File Structure & Paths
docs.text:
• Repository configuration: ~/dotfiles/bat/config
  • Target symlink: ~/.config/bat/config -> ~/dotfiles/bat/config
  • Debian binary: /usr/bin/batcat
  • Local symlink: ~/.local/bin/bat -> /usr/bin/batcat
  • Shell alias: alias cat='batcat' (configured in ~/dotfiles/zsh/zshrc_aliases)

docs.title: Configuration (config)
docs.text:
The active configuration resides in ~/.config/bat/config:

--style=header
--color=always
--wrap=never
--paging=never
--tabs=4

docs.title: Parameter Breakdown
docs.text:
• --style=header: Displays a compact header containing the file path and file type metadata above the file contents, omitting line number grids to keep terminal output clean and easily selectable for copying.
  • --color=always: Guarantees syntax highlighting is rendered even when piping or redirecting stdout where color tags are accepted.
  • --wrap=never: Prevents long lines of code from auto-wrapping across multiple visual rows, maintaining formatting integrity.
  • --paging=never: Emulates traditional cat by streaming output directly to the terminal stdout without piping into a pager like less. This eliminates extra keypresses (q) when viewing short files or running shell scripts.
  • --tabs=4: Standardizes tab stop indentation to 4 characters.

docs.title: Debian Packaging & Binary Resolution
docs.text:
On Debian and Ubuntu systems, the executable binary is packaged as batcat by the package manager (apt install bat) to prevent naming collisions with a legacy Debian package.

To provide a seamless workflow across different distributions and tools:

  1. Local Symlink: The dotfiles deployment script creates a symlink in ~/.local/bin/bat pointing to /usr/bin/batcat.
  2. Shell Alias: alias cat='batcat' in ~/.zshrc_aliases replaces default cat calls transparently.
  3. Plain Cat Fallback: When pure unformatted POSIX cat behavior is required, invoke \cat or /bin/cat.

docs.title: Common Commands & Usage Patterns
docs.text:
# View file with syntax highlighting and file header
cat file.py
bat file.py

# View with full line numbers and git modifications grid
bat --style=full file.py

# Highlight piped input explicitly specifying language
curl -s https://api.github.com | bat -l json

# Inspect Git diff modifications directly in the file
bat --diff file.rs

# List available syntax highlighting themes
bat --list-themes

docs.title: btop Resource Monitor
docs.text: btop is a GPU/CPU/Memory/Disk/Network terminal resource monitor configured with transparent background rendering and automated dynamic color theming generated by Matugen.

docs.title: File Structure & Paths
docs.text:
• Repository configuration: ~/dotfiles/btop/btop.conf
  • Local configuration symlink: ~/.config/btop/btop.conf -> ~/dotfiles/btop/btop.conf
  • Custom themes directory: ~/.config/btop/themes/
  • Active dynamic theme symlink: ~/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme -> ~/.config/themes/current/btop.theme
  • Automation setup script: ~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-btop-matugen.sh

docs.title: Dynamic Matugen Integration
docs.text:
btop inherits the active desktop color palette generated by Matugen from the current wallpaper:

Wallpaper Image (.png / .jpg)
          |
          v
   [ matugen image ]
          |
          v (evaluates ~/.config/matugen/templates/btop.theme)
~/.config/themes/current/btop.theme
          |
          v (symlink)
~/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme
          |
          v (consumed by)
btop (color_theme = "matugen", theme_background = False)

docs.title: Key Theme Settings in btop.conf
docs.text:
• color_theme = "matugen": Instructs btop to load the dynamic theme created by Matugen.
  • theme_background = False: Disables hardcoded opaque background rendering, enabling seamless background transparency and blur from Alacritty and Hyprland.
  • truecolor = True: Enables full 24-bit RGB color depth.

docs.title: Automated Theme Deployment
docs.text:
To initialize or refresh the btop dynamic theme, run:

~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-btop-matugen.sh

Whenever wallpapers are changed via the Quickshell Control Center, ~/.config/themes/apply-matugen.sh automatically re-renders btop.theme alongside all other desktop components.

docs.title: Key Settings & Presets
docs.text:
• Update rate: 2000ms (update_ms = 2000).
  • Process sorting: Sorted by CPU usage in descending order (proc_sorting = "cpu lazy", proc_reversed = True).
  • Presets: Quick layout profiles configured via presets in btop.conf (switchable using keys 1 through 9).

docs.title: Fastfetch Configuration
docs.text: Fastfetch is a lightweight, ultra-fast system information tool configured to display system hardware, environment telemetry, and desktop branding across Alacritty and other terminal sessions.

docs.title: File Structure & Paths
docs.text:
• Repository configuration: ~/dotfiles/fastfetch/config.jsonc
  • Custom logo art: ~/dotfiles/fastfetch/logo.txt
  • Target symlink: ~/.config/fastfetch -> ~/dotfiles/fastfetch

docs.title: Layout & Visual Architecture
docs.text: The configuration leverages custom braille ASCII art alongside structured telemetry modules styled with the system's red primary accent:

docs.title: 1. Logo Section
docs.text:
• Type: File-based logo sourced from ~/.config/fastfetch/logo.txt.
  • Art style: High-density Unicode/Braille graphic emblem.
  • Color: Pure red ("1": "red").
  • Spacing: 4 characters of right-side padding to separate art from text keys.

docs.title: 2. Display and Bar Formatting
docs.text:
• Separator: Custom arrow delimiter colored red.
  • Progress Bars: Dual-line glyph bars (━ elapsed, ─ remaining) enclosed in bracket borders [ ] for graphical representation of:
  • System Memory (RAM) utilization.
  • Root disk partition capacity (used / total (percentage)).
  • Battery charge level and AC power status.

docs.title: 3. Displayed Modules
docs.text:
• User & Host: user@host with custom color formatting.
  • Operating System: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (Trixie) x86_64.
  • Kernel: Active Linux kernel build and architecture.
  • Uptime: Session elapsed time.
  • Packages: Total dpkg package count.
  • Shell: Current interactive shell binary (Zsh Shell Configuration).
  • Window Manager: Hyprland Compositor Architecture version and protocol.
  • Hardware: CPU model and maximum frequency, integrated GPU chipset.
  • Memory & Storage: Real-time RAM and storage consumption.
  • Battery: Charge percentage and charging status.
  • Terminal Palette: 8 circular color swatches positioned at the base, reflecting the active Matugen Color Palette.

docs.title: Execution & Usage
docs.text:
To invoke fastfetch using this configuration:

fastfetch

Fastfetch can also be hooked into your interactive shell greeting inside .zshrc (see Zsh Configuration).

docs.title: Matugen Dynamic Theming Engine
docs.text: Matugen is the Material You (Material Design 3) color palette generator used in this desktop environment. It extracts harmonic color palettes from wallpaper images and propagates them to all active UI components through dynamic templates.

docs.title: Architectural Role and Store
docs.text:
• Engine Configuration: ~/.config/matugen/config.toml (version-controlled in ~/dotfiles/matugen/config.toml).
  • Template Repository: ~/.config/matugen/templates/ contains component-specific template files.
  • Central Theme Store: Output files are rendered directly into ~/.config/themes/current/, which acts as the single source of truth for the entire desktop.
Wallpaper Image (.png / .jpg)
          |
          v
   [ matugen image ]
          |
          v  (processes ~/.config/matugen/templates/)
~/.config/themes/current/
   ├── alacritty.toml  --> read by ~/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml
   ├── wofi.css        --> imported by ~/.config/wofi/style.css
   ├── waybar.css      --> imported by ~/.config/waybar/colors.css
   ├── kitty.conf      --> included by ~/.config/kitty/kitty.conf
   ├── hyprland.conf   --> sourced by Hyprland for active/inactive borders
   ├── hyprlock.conf   --> sourced by ~/.config/hypr/hyprlock.conf
   ├── btop.theme       --> linked by ~/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme
   ├── gtk-3.0.css     --> linked by ~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css
   ├── gtk-4.0.css     --> linked by ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css
   ├── spicetify.ini   --> linked by ~/.config/spicetify/Themes/matugen/color.ini
   ├── steam.css       --> linked by ~/.config/AdwSteamGtk/custom.css
   └── palette.json    --> consumed by Quickshell Control Center & Widgets

docs.title: Configuration (config.toml)
docs.text:

# Matugen is the color generator; ~/.config/themes is the central theme store.

mode = "dark"
type = "scheme-tonal-spot"
source_color_index = 0
scheme_tonal_spot_cutoff = 0.15
scheme_contrast = 1.0

[templates.waybar]
input_path = "~/.config/matugen/templates/waybar.css"
output_path = "~/.config/themes/current/waybar.css"

docs.title: Themed GTK Applications Suite
docs.text: The generated stylesheets dynamically theme classic and modern GTK applications to match the active desktop palette:

docs.title: Core Color Roles
docs.text:
Each template uses standardized Material Design 3 tokens:

  • colors.background.default.hex: Deep primary canvas background.
  • colors.surface.default.hex: Floating surface and card backdrop.
  • colors.surface_container.default.hex: Inactive inputs and container elements.
  • colors.surface_bright.default.hex: Subtle highlight outlines and borders.
  • colors.primary.default.hex: Main accent color, active borders, and focus rings.
  • colors.primary_container.default.hex: Low-contrast selection backgrounds.
  • colors.on_surface.default.hex: Primary text and foreground iconography.
  • colors.on_surface_variant.default.hex: Secondary text, metadata, and hints.
  • colors.outline.default.hex: Structural dividers and borders.
  • colors.error.default.hex: Destructive actions and critical warnings.
  • colors.tertiary.default.hex: Auxiliary highlights, charging states, and indicators.

docs.title: CLI Usage and Manual Palette Generation
docs.text:
To generate a new palette from any wallpaper image:

# Preview extracted palette without writing files
matugen image "/path/to/wallpaper.jpg" --mode dark --dry-run --show-colors

# Generate palette in dark mode
matugen image "/path/to/wallpaper.jpg" --mode dark --source-color-index 0

# Generate palette in light mode
matugen image "/path/to/wallpaper.jpg" --mode light --source-color-index 0

docs.title: Centralized Theme Dispatcher (apply-matugen.sh)
docs.text:
The environment provides ~/.config/themes/apply-matugen.sh to coordinate multi-component reloads and mode persistence:

# Apply with current wallpaper and specific mode
~/.config/themes/apply-matugen.sh "" light
~/.config/themes/apply-matugen.sh "" dark

Optionally adjust the contrast level using --contrast: 

# Increase contrast for accessibility or higher distinction (-1.0 to 1.0)
matugen image "/path/to/wallpaper.jpg" --mode dark --contrast 0.2

docs.title: Privileged Applications Theming (sudo / root)
docs.text:
By default, applications executed with sudo (such as administrative tools, file managers, or system monitors) read configuration files from /root/.config/ and do not inherit user-level CSS overrides.

To synchronize your active Matugen theme with the root user:

sudo ~/dotfiles/scripts/sync-root-theme.sh

docs.title: Mechanism and Persistence:
docs.text:
1. Creates /root/.config/gtk-3.0/ and /root/.config/gtk-4.0/.
  2. Configures Adwaita-dark preference in /root/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini.
  3. Symlinks root GTK stylesheets directly to the user's central theme store:
  4. /root/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css -> ~/.config/themes/current/gtk-3.0.css
  5. /root/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css -> ~/.config/themes/current/gtk-4.0.css
  6. Symlinks root btop monitor theme (/root/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme).

Because these are live symlinks targeting ~/.config/themes/current/, subsequent wallpaper or palette changes made via Quickshell will automatically reflect in root applications without re-executing the synchronization script.

docs.title: Synchronization & Cleanup Flags
docs.text:
The sync-root-theme.sh utility provides flags to manage synchronization or easily restore default themes:

Flag Privilege Description --sync (default) sudo Synchronize root GTK and btop themes from active user theme. --cleanup-user User Revert user GTK3 and GTK4 stylesheets to system defaults. --cleanup-root sudo Remove root theme symlinks and restore original settings. --cleanup-all sudo Revert both user and root configurations to factory defaults. 
# Revert user theme only (no sudo required)
~/dotfiles/scripts/sync-root-theme.sh --cleanup-user

# Revert root theme only
sudo ~/dotfiles/scripts/sync-root-theme.sh --cleanup-root

# Revert both user and root to system defaults
sudo ~/dotfiles/scripts/sync-root-theme.sh --cleanup-all

docs.title: Steam Client Theming
docs.text: The Steam desktop client is integrated into the dynamic Material You theming pipeline using Matugen templates and AdwSteamGtk (Adwaita-for-Steam). This pipeline extracts harmonic colors from the active desktop wallpaper and renders custom CSS variables for Steam's interface, covering window surfaces, headerbars, popovers, sidebars, cards, and accent highlights.

docs.title: File Structure & Paths
docs.text:
• Template source: ~/dotfiles/matugen/templates/steam.css (symlinked into ~/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css)
  • Engine mapping: ~/dotfiles/matugen/config.toml ([templates.steam])
  • Central theme store output: ~/.config/themes/current/steam.css
  • AdwSteamGtk custom stylesheet: ~/.config/AdwSteamGtk/custom.css -> ~/.config/themes/current/steam.css
  • Flatpak AdwSteamGtk custom stylesheet: ~/.var/app/io.github.Foldex.AdwSteamGtk/config/AdwSteamGtk/custom.css -> ~/.config/themes/current/steam.css
  • Deployment automation script: ~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-steam-matugen.sh
  • Dotfiles deployment routine: ~/dotfiles/install.sh

docs.title: Dynamic Matugen Architecture
docs.text:
Steam theming operates through the central theme store and automated post-processing hooks:

Wallpaper Image (.png / .jpg)
          |
          v
   [ matugen image ]
          |
          v (evaluates ~/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css)
~/.config/themes/current/steam.css
          |
          +--> (symlink) ~/.config/AdwSteamGtk/custom.css
          |
          v (post_hook)
adwaita-steam-gtk -i (or flatpak run io.github.Foldex.AdwSteamGtk -i)
          |
          v (injects CSS into)
Steam Client UI (Library, Friends, Settings, Overlays)

docs.title: 1. Matugen Template (matugen/templates/steam.css)
docs.text:

    --adw-accent-fg-rgb: {{ colors.on_primary.default.red }} {{ colors.on_primary.default.green }} {{ colors.on_primary.default.blue }};

docs.title: 2. Matugen Mapping (matugen/config.toml)
docs.text:
The engine config monitors the template, outputs to ~/.config/themes/current/steam.css, and runs the installation hook:

[templates.steam]
input_path = "~/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css"
output_path = "~/.config/themes/current/steam.css"
post_hook = "adwaita-steam-gtk -i >/dev/null 2>&1 || flatpak run io.github.Foldex.AdwSteamGtk -i >/dev/null 2>&1 || true"

docs.title: Step 1: Install AdwSteamGtk
docs.text:
AdwSteamGtk manages the Adwaita skin injection for Steam. Install it using Flatpak (recommended) or build from source:

# Recommended Flatpak installation
flatpak install flathub io.github.Foldex.AdwSteamGtk

docs.title: Step 2: Enable Custom CSS in AdwSteamGtk
docs.text:
1. Launch AdwSteamGtk.
  2. Open Preferences.
  3. Under the Custom CSS section, toggle Custom CSS to Enabled.

Without this setting enabled, AdwSteamGtk ignores custom.css during theme generation.

docs.title: Step 3: Run Deployment Script
docs.text:
Run the automated integration script to link the stylesheet and apply the active desktop theme:

~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-steam-matugen.sh

Alternatively, running ~/dotfiles/install.sh establishes the symlinks automatically during fresh system bootstrapping.

docs.title: Real-time Wallpaper Synchronization
docs.text: When wallpaper transitions occur via Quickshell launcher or control center, matugen image renders all templates. The configured post_hook immediately triggers adwaita-steam-gtk -i, refreshing Steam's active stylesheets without manual intervention.

docs.title: Waybar Status Bar
docs.text: Waybar serves as the primary top status bar in this desktop environment, engineered with a ChromeOS Shelf aesthetic, rounded capsule pills, and seamless IPC communication with Quickshell and the Hyprland compositor.

docs.title: Architecture and File Map
docs.text:
• Live symlink: ~/.config/waybar -> ~/dotfiles/waybar
  • Configuration: ~/.config/waybar/config.jsonc (module layout and actions)
  • Stylesheet: ~/.config/waybar/style.css (visual properties and ChromeOS pill styling)
  • Dynamic Palette: ~/.config/waybar/colors.css (imports ~/.config/themes/current/waybar.css generated by Matugen)
  • Helper Scripts:
    • ~/.config/waybar/scripts/notifications: Reads real-time notification queue state

docs.title: Layout and Modules
docs.text:
Waybar is docked at the top of the display with a height of 36 pixels and bottom corner rounding (border-radius: 0 0 24px 24px):

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| [Launcher] [Workspaces]               [Active Window Title]             [Tray] [Notifs] [Unified System Pill] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 1. Left Section
docs.text:
• custom/launcher: Circular action button styled after the ChromeOS app launcher. Clicking executes qs ipc call launcher toggle to display the Quickshell application drawer.
  • hyprland/workspaces: Pill container with dynamic indicators. Inactive workspaces appear as muted capsule pills, while the active workspace morphs into an accented circular indicator.

docs.title: 2. Center Section
docs.text: • hyprland/window: Displays the active window title with subtle opacity, keeping the central area clean and legible.

docs.title: 3. Right Section
docs.text:
• tray: Wayland system tray for background application icons (icon-size: 14px, spacing: 8px), enclosed in a rounded capsule pill (border-radius: 18px, background: alpha(@text, 0.08), padding: 0 10px) matching the notification bell and quick status indicators. Automatically hides background and margins when empty.
  • Quick Status Indicators (Pills):
    • custom/caffeine: Pill indicator displaying coffee cup glyph (󰅶) when active. Synchronizes with session wake-lock inhibitor via POSIX signal SIGRTMIN+8. Clicking toggles wake-lock state.
    • custom/nightlight: Pill indicator displaying eye glyph (󰈈) when hyprsunset blue-light filter (4000K) is active. Synchronizes via POSIX signal SIGRTMIN+9. Clicking toggles warm filter state.
    • custom/shader: Pill indicator displaying screen shader glyph (󰸉) when Hyprland decoration filter is active. Synchronizes via POSIX signal SIGRTMIN+10. Clicking toggles active shader profile.
    • Styling & Metrics: Indicators render as rounded pills (height: 28px, border-radius: 18px, background: alpha(@text, 0.08)) with asymmetric horizontal padding (padding: 0 13px 0 9px and 0 12px 0 10px) to compensate for font side bearings and maintain exact optical centering.
  • custom/notifications: Notification bell pill connected to Quickshell's notification daemon:
    • Reads unread count from /tmp/qs-notif-count.
    • Receives instant wakeup via POSIX signal SIGRTMIN+1 whenever notifications arrive or dismiss.
    • Clicking invokes qs ipc call notifications toggle.
  • Unified Status Pill: Merged continuous capsule pill containing date, time, audio, network, bluetooth, and battery/power:
    • custom/date: Formatted date (date +'%b %d'), styled as the rounded left edge of the unified pill.
    • clock: Local time format {:%H:%M} with bold typography.
    • pulseaudio: Volume glyphs; click toggles Quickshell Control Center, right-click opens pavucontrol, and mouse wheel scrolling adjusts sink volume using wpctl set-volume.
    • network: Wi-Fi / Ethernet state; click opens Quickshell Control Center.
    • bluetooth: Adapter state and connection count; click opens Quickshell Control Center.
    • battery / custom/power: Charge percentage, charging animations, and battery warnings (laptop) or power state (desktop), styled as the rounded right edge of the unified pill.

docs.title: Integration with Quickshell and Hyprland
docs.text:
Waybar and Quickshell operate in synchronized coexistence:

  1. Vertical Hierarchy:
  2. Waybar occupies the top 36 pixels (height: 36, layer: top).
  3. Quickshell floating toasts and OSDs reserve a topMargin: 46 px, creating an aligned 10 px air gap directly below Waybar's rounded bottom border (see Notifications & OSDs).
  4. IPC Interactivity:
  5. Clicking audio, network, or bluetooth indicators directly opens the One UI Control Center inside Quickshell.
  6. Clicking the launcher circle opens the Quickshell app search matrix without requiring full-screen interruptions.
  7. Real-time Signal Sync (SIGRTMIN+1):
  8. Quickshell writes unread counts to /tmp/qs-notif-count and issues pkill -RTMIN+1 waybar, triggering immediate redraws without CPU polling overhead.

  • @critical: Battery critical threshold (<= 10%).

docs.title: Release Management & SemVer
docs.text: This repository follows Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) and Conventional Commits to automate versioning, release artifacts, and documentation deployment.

docs.title: Versioning Scheme
docs.text:
• MAJOR (vX.0.0): Incompatible architectural overhauls (e.g. switching compositor, complete directory reshuffling).
  • MINOR (v1.X.0): New features, widgets, or apps added backward-compatibly (e.g. adding an OCR tool, new Quickshell modules).
  • PATCH (v1.0.X): Backward-compatible bug fixes, minor CSS styling tweaks, or performance optimizations.

docs.title: How to Trigger a Release
docs.text: You have two convenient ways to cut a new release:

docs.title: Option 1: From Your Terminal (CLI Helper)
docs.text:
Run the included release script in the repository:

# Interactive mode (prompts for patch, minor, major, or custom)
./scripts/release.sh

# Or directly specify the bump type:
./scripts/release.sh patch   # e.g. v1.0.0 -> v1.0.1
./scripts/release.sh minor   # e.g. v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0
./scripts/release.sh major   # e.g. v1.0.0 -> v2.0.0
./scripts/release.sh v1.0.0  # explicit version

The script will: 1. Verify that your git working tree is clean. 2. Determine the next SemVer tag. 3. Create the annotated git tag. 4. Push both main and the new tag to GitHub.

docs.title: Option 2: From GitHub Actions (Web UI)
docs.text:
1. Navigate to your repository on GitHub: https://github.com/zer0sh/dotfiles/actions.
  2. Select the Release & Deploy workflow on the left sidebar.
  3. Click Run workflow.
  4. Choose the bump type (patch, minor, major) or enter a custom version.
  5. Click the green Run workflow button.

docs.title: Automated Pipeline (What Happens on Release)
docs.text:
When a release tag is pushed (v*.*.*):

flowchart LR
    A["Git Tag (v1.0.0)"] --> B["GitHub Actions"]
    B --> C["Package Archives (.tar.gz & .zip)"]
    B --> D["Generate Release Notes (Conventional Commits)"]
    C --> E["Publish GitHub Release"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["Deploy Wiki to GitHub Pages"]
  1. Release Notes: GitHub automatically categorizes commits into Features, Bug Fixes, and Maintenance based on Conventional Commits.
  2. Packaged Assets: Generates clean dotfiles-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz and dotfiles-vX.Y.Z.zip archives attached to the release for easy distribution or disaster recovery.
  3. Wiki Deployment: Compiles and deploys the latest MkDocs documentation to zer0sh.github.io/dotfiles.

docs.title: Dotfiles Workflow & Architecture
docs.text: This guide explains how configuration files are structured between your active system and the version-controlled repository on GitHub.

docs.title: Direct Source of Truth Philosophy
docs.text:
• Hyprland: ~/.config/hypr is a real physical directory (not a symlink). You can edit configuration files directly in place without risk of symlink breakage or intermediate layer issues (see Hyprland Architecture).
  • Quickshell: ~/.config/quickshell is also maintained directly on the system for instant QML hot-reloading (see Quickshell Overview).
  • Dotfiles Repository: ~/dotfiles serves as the Git repository and backup hub connected to github.com/zer0sh/dotfiles.
  • Symlinked Applications: Modular components like Alacritty, Zsh, and Fastfetch link their active system paths directly to ~/dotfiles/.

docs.title: How to Backup Hyprland Changes
docs.text:
Whenever you test and stabilize adjustments in your Hyprland configuration and want to commit them to your repository:

  1. Copy live configuration into the dotfiles directory: 
    cp -r ~/.config/hypr/* ~/dotfiles/hypr/
  2. Review diffs and create atomic commits: Follow Conventional Commits standards as documented in Release Management & SemVer: 
    cd ~/dotfiles
git status
git add hypr/
git commit -m "feat(hypr): describe your changes"
  3. Push to GitHub: 
    git push origin main

docs.title: Documentation Deployment (MkDocs)
docs.text:

cd ~/dotfiles
mkdocs serve

To build and deploy changes directly to GitHub Pages:

cd ~/dotfiles
mkdocs gh-deploy

(Note: Pushing to main also automatically triggers the GitHub Actions workflow defined in .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml, as detailed in Release Management & SemVer).

docs.title: Hyprland Architecture
docs.text: Hyprland is organized using a strict modular approach. The primary hyprland.conf does not define keybindings or individual properties directly; it acts exclusively as an orchestrator using source = directives.

docs.title: Directory & File Structure
docs.text:
~/.config/hypr/
├── hyprland.conf         # Master entrypoint (imports sub-modules only)
├── binds.conf            # Keyboard shortcuts and mouse actions
├── monitors.conf         # Screen layouts and refresh rates (nwg-displays)
├── workspaces.conf       # Virtual desktop allocations
├── autostart.conf        # Startup services and daemons (exec-once)
├── animations.conf       # Bezier curves and window movement dynamics
├── decoration.conf       # Borders, shadows, blur, and gaps
├── miscellaneous.conf    # Keyboard repeat rate and layout behavior
├── window.conf           # Window rules (windowrule / windowrulev2)
├── hyprlock.conf         # Lock screen layout and theming
├── hypridle.conf         # Idle management and power saving
├── scripts/              # Executable shell helpers (OCR, screenshots, filters)
└── shaders/              # Custom GLSL post-processing shaders

docs.title: Master Entrypoint (hyprland.conf)
docs.text:
# Monitor layout managed by nwg-displays
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/monitors.conf

source = $HOME/.config/hypr/variables.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/binds.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/window.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/decoration.conf

# Centralized palette generated by the active theme
source = $HOME/.config/themes/current/hyprland.conf

source = $HOME/.config/hypr/animations.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/miscellaneous.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/autostart.conf

docs.title: Screen Locking & Idle Management (Hyprlock & Hypridle)
docs.text: Session security and power conservation are handled natively within the Hyprland ecosystem using Hyprlock (fast, graphical Wayland screen locker) and Hypridle (Wayland-native idle daemon).

docs.title: File Locations & Symlinks

  • Hypridle configuration: ~/dotfiles/hypr/hypridle.conf -> ~/.config/hypr/hypridle.conf
  • Dynamic color palette: ~/.config/themes/current/hyprlock.conf (generated by Matugen)
  • Keybindings definition: ~/dotfiles/hypr/binds.conf
  • Autostart registration: ~/dotfiles/hypr/autostart.conf

docs.title: Hyprlock Architecture
docs.text: Hyprlock generates a real-time frosted glass lock screen that adapts dynamically to the current wallpaper and active Material You color palette.

docs.title: 1. Dynamic Theming (Matugen Integration)
docs.text:
Color tokens are evaluated by Matugen and imported directly into hyprlock.conf:

source = /home/zero/.config/themes/current/hyprlock.conf

Available color roles include: * $accentColorPurple: Primary accent used for borders and validation states. * $bgColorSecondary: Inner background container for the input field. * $textColor: High-contrast font color for clock and labels. * $textColorDanger: Error state indicator for incorrect password attempts. * $accentColorAttention: Warning color indicating Caps Lock activation.

docs.title: 2. Visual Elements & Widgets
docs.text:
$font = JetBrainsMono Nerd Font

general {
  hide_cursor = true
  fail_timeout = 1000
}

# TIME (Large digital clock)
label {
  text = $TIME
  color = $textColor
  font_size = 90
  font_family = $font
  position = 0, 200
  halign = center
  valign = center
}

# DATE (Localized date header)
label {
  monitor =
  text = cmd[update:43200000] date +"%A, %d %B %Y"
  color = $textColor
  font_size = 25
  font_family = $font
  position = 0, 110
  halign = center
  valign = center
}

docs.title: 3. Password Input Field
docs.text:
The password holder is centered below the time and date, configured with real-time feedback:

input-field {
  monitor =
  size = 300, 60
  outline_thickness = 4
  dots_size = 0.2
  dots_spacing = 0.2
  dots_center = true
  outer_color = $accentColorPurple
  inner_color = $bgColorSecondary
  font_color = $textColor
  fade_on_empty = false
  placeholder_text = <span foreground="##$textColorHex"><i>󰌾 Logged in as </i><span foreground="##$accentColorPurpleHex">$USER</span></span>
  hide_input = false
  check_color = $accentColorPurple
  fail_color = $textColorDanger
  fail_text = <i>$FAIL <b>($ATTEMPTS)</b></i>
  capslock_color = $accentColorAttention
  position = 0, -30
  halign = center
  valign = center
}
  • Live Feedback: Outlines animate on input, flash red ($textColorDanger) with attempt counts upon authentication failure, and shift to $accentColorAttention when Caps Lock is active.
  • Placeholder: Displays the active username dynamically using Pango markup with icon badge 󰌾.

docs.title: 4. Background Rendering
docs.text:
background {
  path = screenshot
  blur_passes = 2
  brightness = 0.56
}
  • Screenshot Capture: path = screenshot grabs the active Wayland framebuffer upon invocation.
  • Frosted Glass Blur: Evaluates 2 blur passes and dims brightness to 0.56 to obscure sensitive content while preserving ambient desktop aesthetics.

docs.title: Hypridle Daemon Configuration
docs.text:
hypridle runs as a persistent background daemon launched from autostart.conf:

exec-once = hypridle

docs.title: Configuration (hypridle.conf)
docs.text:
general {
    before_sleep_cmd = hyprlock
    after_sleep_cmd = hyprctl dispatch dpms on
    ignore_dbus_inhibit = false
    lock_cmd = hyprlock
}

listener {
    timeout = 300
    on-timeout = hyprlock
}
  • Sleep Safeguard: before_sleep_cmd = hyprlock guarantees the session locks immediately before system suspend or hibernation.
  • Wake Recovery: after_sleep_cmd = hyprctl dispatch dpms on restores display power as soon as the system resumes.
  • Inactivity Rule: timeout = 300 automatically triggers hyprlock after 5 minutes of continuous user inactivity.

docs.title: Quickshell & Control Center
docs.text: Quickshell is the Wayland-native QML widget framework driving this desktop environment. It provides a One UI inspired control center featuring translucent cards, rounded pill toggles, and reactive sliders on top of the Hyprland compositor.

docs.title: Modules Overview
docs.text:
• Control Center (modules/controlcenter/):
  • Layout Architecture: Balanced two-column grid layout featuring a left widgets column (Analog Clock, Weather, Media Player) and a right control matrix (4x3 quick toggle grid alongside vertical glassmorphic sliders).
  • Analog Clock Widget (AnalogClockWidget.qml): Canvas-based analog dial with dynamic hour and minute hands, digital time readout, and localized English weekday and calendar date.
  • Weather Widget (WeatherWidget.qml): Live atmospheric conditions, ambient temperature, location label, and relative humidity fetched via OpenWeather API in English.
  • Vertical Sliders Card: Frosted glassmorphic card housing vertical reactive sliders for PipeWire audio volume and brightnessctl display backlight.
  • Quick Toggles (4x3 Grid): Rounded pill buttons for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, DND, Airplane Mode, Caffeine, Power Profiles, Night Light, Screen Shaders, Audio outputs, Dynamic Theming, Energy, and Wallpaper selection.
  • Energy & Performance Dashboard (BatterySection.qml): Dedicated hardware metrics subpage displaying charge percentage, discharge rates, full charge estimates, battery health state, power draw, charge cycles, and power profile presets (Power Saver, Balanced, Performance).
  • Waybar Sync: Seamless bidirectional state sync between quick toggles (Caffeine, Night Light, Shader) and top status bar indicators using POSIX signals.
  • Notifications & Control Center Integration (modules/controlcenter/, modules/notifications/):
  • Native DBus notification server (org.freedesktop.Notifications) managed by NotificationService.qml.
  • Top-center floating toast layer (NotificationToastLayer.qml) with smooth downward entrance animations.
  • Collapsible notifications card embedded directly inside the Control Center featuring the title Notifications • ( # ), rotating toggle chevron, quick "Clear all" action, empty placeholder state, and scrollable notification list.
  • Waybar notification bell triggers qs ipc call notifications toggle, opening the Control Center with the notifications card smoothly expanded.
  • Full design parameters and easing curves detailed in the Notifications & OSDs Guide.
  • Clipboard Manager (modules/clipboard/):
  • Visual history and search for text and images integrated with cliphist.
  • Keyboard access mapped via Hyprland Keybindings.
  • DeskClock & Calendar (modules/deskclock/, modules/calendar/):
  • Ambient desktop clock surface and expandable calendar panel with date navigation.
  • Mini Music Player (modules/osd/MiniPlayer.qml):
  • Compact MPRIS playback controller triggered with SUPER + M as defined in Hyprland Keybindings.
  • Application Launcher & Theme Selector (modules/launcher/):
  • Fast native application runner and app drawer complementing Wofi Launcher.
  • Interactive theme carousel (>theme mode) displaying theme preview cards (ThemeCard.qml), active status badges, and an integrated top header bar with title and a quick Light Mode / Dark Mode switch.
  • Synchronized with Matugen and persisted in ~/.config/themes/current/mode.

docs.title: Dynamic Palette & Glassmorphism Integration
docs.text:
Quickshell widgets consume Material Design 3 tokens generated dynamically by Matugen:

  • Token source: ~/.config/themes/current/palette.json
  • Theme loader: Theme.qml loads colors reactively, allowing instantaneous UI repaints when wallpapers or light/dark modes change without restarting the shell.
  • Centralized Glassmorphism: Standardized transparency properties (Root.Theme.glassPanel with opacity 0.55 and Root.Theme.glassCard with opacity 0.85) unified across the DeskClock widget, launcher floating cards, and notifications.
  • Semantic roles: Surface containers, primary accents, text variants, and outline borders are mapped directly to QML elements.

# Validate QML syntax without restarting
~/.config/quickshell/restart-quickshell.sh --validate

# Restart Quickshell live
~/.config/quickshell/restart-quickshell.sh

docs.title: Floating Launcher & Animated Wallpaper Carousel
docs.text: Quickshell implements a floating bottom-center application launcher and animated wallpaper selector inspired by Caelestia Shell. The component is integrated directly with Wayland layershell, Matugen color extraction, and hardware-accelerated QML transitions.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The system consists of two coordinated Quickshell modules:

  1. Floating Launcher (modules/launcher/):
  2. Placed on WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay.
  3. Horizontally centered at the bottom of the screen with a 28 px bottom margin.
  4. Translucent dark surface with rounded corners (22 px radius), subtle border highlight, and outer glow.
  5. Search input at the bottom with real-time mode detection:
    • Application Mode (default): Lists system desktop entries with official icons, titles, and descriptions.
    • Command / Actions Mode (>): Activated by typing > to expose system commands.
    • Wallpaper Carousel (>wallpaper / SUPER + W): Horizontal card carousel featuring 16:9 previews, active wallpaper glow, and a local file explorer.
  6. Desktop Background Engine (modules/background/Background.qml):
  7. Placed on WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Background on all connected displays (Quickshell.screens).
  8. Implements a double-buffer (ping-pong) layer switching architecture, guaranteeing reliable consecutive wallpaper transitions without QML property binding degradation.
  9. Manages smooth cross-image animations, replacing static background setters like swaybg.
  10. Applies the "Zoom & Blur" (Emergence) transition:
    • Outgoing wallpaper scales from 1.0 to 1.15 while fading opacity from 1.0 to 0.0 in 750 ms (Easing.InOutQuad).
    • Incoming wallpaper scales from 0.88 to 1.0 while fading opacity from 0.0 to 1.0 in 750 ms (Easing.InOutQuad).
  11. Triggers apply-matugen.sh asynchronously to regenerate system palettes across Hyprland, Waybar, Alacritty, and Quickshell.

│   ├── background/

docs.title: 1. Application Search Mode
docs.text: When the search input is empty or contains standard text: * Lists all installed .desktop applications discovered by list-apps.py. * Shows application icon, title in bold, and comment / category description. * High-Contrast Selection Feedback: * Active item receives a vibrant translucent primary tint (rgba(primary, 0.22)) and 1.5 px glowing primary border. * Vertical accent pill indicator on the left border. * Prominent [ 󰌑 Enter ] badge on the right edge. * Dynamic icon and title scale expansion. * Keyboard navigation: Up / Down arrows move selection with automatic viewport positioning (positionViewAtIndex), Enter executes the application and closes the launcher, Escape cancels.

docs.title: 2. Action / Command Mode (>)
docs.text: Typing > filters available system commands: * Wallpaper Carousel: Enters the horizontal wallpaper picker carousel (>wallpaper). * Theme Carousel: Enters the horizontal visual theme picker carousel (>theme). * Light Mode / Dark Mode: Switches Matugen generation mode. * Lock Screen: Locks session using hyprlock. * Sleep / Suspend: Suspends the machine to RAM (systemctl suspend). * Restart System / Shut Down: Session reboot and power-off actions.

docs.title: 3. Wallpaper Carousel Mode
docs.text: Typing >wallpaper or pressing SUPER + W opens the horizontal carousel: * Expanded floating card container (1080 px width, 340 px height, 24 px radius) offering generous horizontal and vertical headroom. * Caelestia Shell Containment & Edge Fade Overlays: * Strict clipping (clip: true) enforced across the floating dock card, content viewport, and horizontal list view, eliminating lateral overflow beyond container boundaries. * Left and right 32 px horizontal gradient fade overlays that smoothly blend scrollable cards into the dark dock background without hard cutoffs. * Displays 16:9 cards (224x214 px with 120 px thumbnail height) generated from /home/zero/Pictures/walls/ and cached in ~/.cache/wallpapers/. * Hover & Selection Styling: * Dynamic elevation: Cards lift upward by -5 px on hover (-2 px on keyboard selection). * Smooth scale: Subtle 1.05 expansion on hover (1.03 on keyboard selection) with Easing.OutCubic. * Internal thumbnail zoom: 16:9 thumbnail expands to 1.05 within rounded bounds. * Vibrant halo glow: Border widens to 2 px with primary accent color and expanded glow margins. * Active Badge: The currently active desktop wallpaper is highlighted with an "Active" badge and a focused double border. * Add Local File Card: Positioned at the end of the carousel. Clicking or pressing Enter opens a native file dialog (zenity) to import external images, automatically caching thumbnails and applying the wallpaper.

docs.title: 4. Theme Carousel Mode
docs.text: Typing >theme or >tema, clicking "Theme" in the Control Center, or executing qs ipc call launcher theme opens the horizontal theme carousel: * Reuses the same 1080x340 px floating container and smooth horizontal scroll architecture as the wallpaper carousel. * Visual Theme Cards (ThemeCard.qml): * Displays 224x214 px cards with a dedicated 120 px preview container showcasing an interface mockup for each palette. * Preview includes a miniature header, active primary widget, slider with active track, accent chip, and 5 color swatches (primary, primaryContainer, surfaceContainerHigh, connected, textPrimary). * Palette colors resolve via explicit Qt.color conversion, ensuring accurate rendering across both static palettes and dynamic Matugen extractions. * An "Active" badge dynamically marks the currently applied theme. * Interactive Behavior: * Selecting a card applies the theme instantly via Theme.currentTheme, persists it to ~/.config/quickshell/current-theme, triggers apply-theme.sh or apply-matugen.sh across the system, and closes the launcher. * Full keyboard support with Left / Right navigation, Enter to apply, and text filtering (e.g. >theme cobalt).

docs.title: IPC Commands and Keybindings
docs.text:
The launcher and background engine expose IPC endpoints:

# Toggle application launcher
qs ipc call launcher toggle

# Open wallpaper carousel directly
qs ipc call launcher wallpaper

# Open theme carousel directly
qs ipc call launcher theme
qs ipc call themepicker show

# Navigate selection via IPC
qs ipc call launcher next
qs ipc call launcher prev
qs ipc call launcher activate

# Filter commands or text via IPC
qs ipc call launcher search ">"

# Set wallpaper programmatically with animated transition
qs ipc call wallpaper set "/path/to/image.png"

# Hide launcher
qs ipc call launcher hide

docs.text:

  • SUPER + W: Invokes qs ipc call launcher wallpaper to present the wallpaper carousel.

docs.title: Notifications & OSDs
docs.text: This guide details the architecture, screen positioning, and animation dynamics for floating notification toasts and on-screen display (OSD) cards (Volume, Brightness, Music, and Mini Player) in Quickshell running on the Hyprland compositor.

docs.title: Design Parameters and Dynamics
docs.text:
All floating indicators follow a standardized behavioral contract:

  1. Screen Placement: Top of the screen, horizontally centered (anchors.top: true, anchors.horizontalCenter: parent.horizontalCenter).
  2. Top Margin: topMargin: 46 px (reserves a comfortable visual gap beneath Waybar's 36 px height).
  3. Theming: Colors, translucency, and borders are rendered using Matugen Dynamic Palette Tokens (surface_container, outline, on_surface).
  4. Entrance Animation (Downward Slide):
  5. Translates from _slideY: -28 to 0 over 260–280 ms using Easing.OutCubic acceleration.
  6. Fades in opacity from 0 to 1 over 220 ms using Easing.OutQuad.
  7. Queue Dynamics: When a new notification arrives, it occupies the top slot and fluidly pushes older active notifications downward using move: Transition.
  8. Dismissal Animation: Gently moves upward (to: -20) and fades out (opacity: 0) before unmounting from the model.

docs.title: Adjusting Vertical Distance
docs.text:
Edit topMargin in the container Item or toastCol: 

anchors.topMargin: 46 // Increase to push further down, decrease to lift closer to bar

docs.text:

NumberAnimation {
    target: osdCard; property: "_slideY"
    from: -28; to: 0; duration: 260; easing.type: Easing.OutCubic
}

docs.title: Alacritty Configuration
docs.text: Alacritty serves as the primary terminal emulator in this environment, running the Zsh Shell with instant live configuration reloading and tight integration with the Matugen Dynamic Theming Engine.

docs.title: File Locations
docs.text:
• Repository source: ~/dotfiles/alacritty/alacritty.toml
  • Target symlink: ~/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml
  • Imported color palette: ~/.config/themes/current/alacritty.toml

docs.title: Dynamic Theme Integration (Matugen)
docs.text:
Alacritty delegates color palette definitions to an externally managed file generated by Matugen:

[general]
import = ["/home/zero/.config/themes/current/alacritty.toml"]
live_config_reload = true

docs.title: Live Update Workflow
docs.text:
1. Matugen processes the current desktop wallpaper or the manual theme selected via the Quickshell Control Center.
  2. It evaluates the template located at ~/.config/matugen/templates/alacritty.toml against the generated color roles.
  3. The resulting palette is written to ~/.config/themes/current/alacritty.toml.
  4. Because live_config_reload = true is enabled, all active Alacritty windows immediately update their colors without restarting or interrupting active shell sessions.

docs.title: Visual Settings & Typography
docs.text:
[window]
opacity = 0.92
padding = { x = 15, y = 15 }

[cursor]

  • Font: BlexMono Nerd Font (Bold weight) for crisp glyph rendering and comprehensive icon support, matching Wofi Launcher.

docs.text: Vim serves as the modal terminal text editor in this environment, configured with modern UI ergonomics, SynthWave '84 syntax highlighting, vim-airline status bar theming, NERDTree file explorer, and full system clipboard synchronization under Debian and Wayland.

docs.title: System Dependencies (Debian / Wayland)
docs.text:
To enable seamless copy/paste integration with Wayland and manage plugins, the following packages are required on Debian:

sudo apt install vim-gtk3 wl-clipboard
  • vim-gtk3: Replaces the default vim.basic binary with a version compiled with +clipboard and +xterm_clipboard. This activates set clipboard=unnamedplus in terminal sessions without launching a graphical window.
  • wl-clipboard: Provides wl-copy and wl-paste command-line tools for native clipboard buffer management in Wayland / Hyprland.
  • git & curl: Required by the vim-plug package manager to fetch and update plugin repositories.

docs.title: Plugin Architecture (vim-plug)
docs.text:

  • preservim/nerdtree: Tree-style directory viewer and file explorer.
  • artanikin/vim-synthwave84: Vibrant 80s neon synthwave color scheme with true color support.
  • vim-airline/vim-airline: Lightweight, customizable bottom statusline.
  • vim-airline/vim-airline-themes: Theme collection for vim-airline (configured to synthwave84).

  • Mouse: Full pointer support for scrolling and cursor positioning across all modes (mouse=a).
  • Clipboard: Centralized synchronization with the system clipboard (clipboard=unnamedplus).

docs.title: Zsh Shell Configuration
docs.text: Zsh serves as the interactive login shell across all terminal sessions (such as Alacritty), optimized for instant startup times, intelligent history handling, asynchronous-like autosuggestions, and streamlined Git integration within the Dotfiles Architecture.

docs.title: File Locations & Symlinks
docs.text:
• Configuration root: ~/dotfiles/zsh/zshrc -> ~/.zshrc
  • Aliases: ~/dotfiles/zsh/zshrc_aliases -> ~/.zshrc_aliases
  • Custom Prompts: ~/dotfiles/zsh/prompts/ -> ~/.zsh/prompts/
  • Plugin storage: ~/.zsh/plugins/ (managed via ~/dotfiles/install.sh, see Dotfiles Workflow)
  • Private overrides: ~/.zshrc_private (local machine only, unversioned)

docs.title: Startup Performance & Completion Cache
docs.text:
To eliminate the latency commonly associated with heavy frameworks like Oh-My-Zsh or Prezto, the configuration implements lightweight, native Zsh mechanisms with a 24-hour cache check on the completion dump:

autoload -Uz compinit
setopt extendedglob
if [[ -n ${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zcompdump(#qN.mh+24) ]]; then
    compinit
else
    compinit -C
fi
  • Cache check (#qN.mh+24): If the compiled completion dump (.zcompdump) was modified within the last 24 hours, compinit -C runs directly, bypassing expensive filesystem scans.
  • Measured startup time: ~120 ms for cold interactive start with all active plugins and completions loaded.

docs.title: Completion Menu & Visual Styling
docs.text:
The completion system is styled to match the dark terminal palette with interactive arrow navigation and detailed process inspection:

  • Tab menu navigation: zstyle ':completion:*' menu select=2 enables interactive visual grid selection upon pressing Tab.
  • Case-insensitive matching: Matches lowercase queries against uppercase files and handles dot/underscore boundaries automatically.
  • Process kill helper: Provides highlighted process listing (PID, %CPU, TTY, TIME, CMD) when running kill <Tab>.
  • Colorization: Synchronized with $LS_COLORS evaluated via dircolors -b.

docs.title: History Configuration & Privacy
docs.text:
HISTSIZE=20000
SAVEHIST=20000
HISTFILE=~/.zsh_history

setopt hist_ignore_all_dups     # Remove older duplicates if a new command is recorded
setopt hist_save_no_dups        # Never write consecutive duplicate entries
setopt hist_ignore_space        # Commands prefixed with leading whitespace are excluded from history
setopt hist_reduce_blanks       # Strip superfluous whitespace before writing
setopt share_history            # Interactively share history across concurrent terminal tabs
setopt inc_append_history       # Append history entries immediately upon command execution

The hist_ignore_space setting enables safe command execution containing tokens, passwords, or secrets by simply prepending a space to the command line.

docs.title: Lightweight Plugin Ecosystem
docs.text:
All plugins are cloned as shallow submodules under ~/.zsh/plugins/ during install.sh without external plugin managers:

  1. zsh-autosuggestions:
  2. Suggests commands as you type based on your shell history and completions.
  3. Keybinding: Ctrl + Space triggers autosuggest-accept.
  4. zsh-history-substring-search:
  5. Type any substring and cycle through previous matches using Up and Down arrow keys.
  6. zsh-syntax-highlighting:
  7. Provides real-time syntax validation (green for valid commands/paths, red for invalid commands).
  8. Loaded strictly as the final plugin to ensure accurate terminal tokenization.
  9. zsh-completions:
  10. Additional third-party completion definitions added to fpath prior to compinit.

docs.title: CLI Integrations
docs.text:
The shell dynamically verifies and activates installed modern CLI utilities:

  • fzf: Activated via eval "$(fzf --zsh)" providing fuzzy reverse search (Ctrl + R) and fuzzy path completion (Ctrl + T).
  • zoxide: Smart directory jumper activated via eval "$(zoxide init zsh)" using the z command.
  • lsd: Modern ls alternative with icons, tree views, and color schemes aliased to ls, ll (lsd -la), and lt (lsd --tree).
  • batcat / bat: Syntax-highlighted pager replacement aliased to cat (see Bat Configuration).

docs.title: Custom Prompts
docs.text: Custom prompts reside in ~/dotfiles/zsh/prompts/ and are registered via Zsh's built-in promptinit system.

docs.title: 1. Minimal (prompt minimal) - Default
docs.text: A fast, single-line prompt featuring: * Compressed path notation (_shrink_path): Converts deep paths like ~/Workspace/personal/project into ~/W/p/project to preserve horizontal terminal width. * Git status (vcs_info): Displays branch name in red, with * for unstaged changes and + for staged changes. * Exit code indicator: Changes prompt symbol to green › on exit 0 and red › [code] on non-zero return codes. * Right prompt (RPROMPT): Displays current timestamp (HH:MM) in muted grey.

docs.title: 2. Macbar (prompt macbar) - Alternative
docs.text: A two-line aesthetic prompt: * Line 1: Full directory path with Git branch badge in brackets. * Line 2: Indented prompt symbol (λ), green on success and red on failure. * Right prompt: Git branch icon (󰊢) and timestamp.
